page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the arm64 architecture. It features 1 dedicated vCPU powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a 4.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor features 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the single-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1783.48 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1018.0. However, due to the single-core limitation, multi-core performance is poor, scoring 1783.48 in stress-ng and 1017.0 in Geekbench. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 11.99 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 7.95 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates weak single-threaded gzip compression at 23.65 GB/sec and poor static web serving throughput at 1.38 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds for a small 135M model reach 45.42 tokens per second for prompt processing and 33.34 tokens per second for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2a-standard-1 offers a low-resource entry point into ARM-based cloud computing, providing dedicated CPU allocation without the shared-core performance degradation of burstable instances. However, the lack of local storage and low multi-threaded performance present clear tradeoffs for resource-intensive applications. This server is best aligned with lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic utility services, simple web serving, and software development or testing environments optimized for the arm64 architecture.
